To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the TCTP gene is expressed in all the stages of the filarial parasite life cycle and is present in the excretions/secretions of the microfilariae, and that the recombinant filarial TCTP has histamine-releasing and inflammatory activity in mice.
the filarial homologues of TCTP are calcium-binding proteins with histamine releasing and inflammatory functions.
the TCTPs of the human filarial parasite Wuchereria bancrotii and its close relative Brugia malayii are calcium-binding proteins that form multimers, and have histamine releasing activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of a novel protein, the TCTP from the human filariae Wuchereria bancrotfi and Brugia malyi.
the identification, cloning, expression and characterization of TCTP homologues from the human filariasis parasites B. malayi, W. bancrofi and Onchocerca volvulus.
the molecular characterization of a calcium-binding protein from the human filariae, W. bancrofi and B. malayi.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TCTPs from B. malay and W. bancroti have a high degree of homology and share common properties with the mammalian TCTPs.
the filarial parasites have evolved their own TCTP gene that has a similar structure, function and localization as that of the mammalian TCTP.
the filarial translationally controlled tumor proteins (fTCTPs) are homologues to mammalian TCTPs and are immunologically and structurally similar.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified and characterized the first TCTPs from the human filariae.
the filarial parasites express a homologue of mammalian TCTP which may have a role as an immune modulatory factor in the inflammatory responses associated with the infection.
we have cloned and expressed the filarial TTPs and have characterized the recombinant proteins in terms of their biochemical properties and biological activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TCTPs are present abundantly in filarial ES products and are immunogenic in humans.
the filarial parasites have a calcium binding TCTP homologue which is expressed in the microfilariae and has histamine releasing and eosinophilic inflammatory functions.
TCTPs are highly conserved proteins in the filarial nematodes, and they may have important functions in these parasites.
